title: Spinal segments and spinal nerves
objective: Describe how the spinal cord is segmented and how spinal nerves leave it.

steps.title: The cord is built in segments
steps.body: The spinal cord is organized into **segments**, grouped by region: cervical (neck), thoracic (chest), lumbar (lower back), and sacral (pelvis). Each segment gives off a pair of **[[spinal nerve|spinal nerves]]**, one per side. Where along this axis a neuron connects tells you roughly which body region it serves.

steps.title: A spinal nerve is a junction
steps.body: Each [[spinal nerve]] forms where two roots join: the **[[dorsal root]]** (sensory, carrying [[afferent]] axons inward) and the **[[ventral root]]** (motor, carrying [[efferent]] axons out). So a spinal nerve is *mixed* — sensory and motor fibers bundled together after the roots merge.

steps.prompt: A spinal nerve carries which fibers?
options: Only sensory fibers, carrying signals inward
Only motor fibers, carrying commands outward
Both: it's mixed, where dorsal and ventral roots join
Neither; a spinal nerve is actually a CNS tract
steps.explanation: The dorsal and ventral roots merge into a mixed spinal nerve. Upstream of the merge, the roots are cleanly separated by function — which the next lesson uses.
